facts.fact: Coore & Crenshaw, opened 1 June 2005; it runs from dune scrub through meadow into Sitka spruce and shore pine forest; no hole on the ocean.

current.subject: A wooden trail-marker post beside a spruce (course chat, developer's call).
current.keep: The trail marker, the course's name in an object.
current.weaknesses: The post and the tree compete side by side; the arrow is tiny.

concepts.name: The Trail Marker
concepts.rationale: One object: a gabled cedar trail post with a Sitka spruce routed into its face and a carved arrow below, standing in dune grass.
references: Sitka spruce forest on the course (fact)
concepts.symbolism: The way on: the post tells you where the trail goes and what you'll find there.
concepts.typography: Alegreya Sans SC: humanist, like park signage.
concepts.strengths: A single tall silhouette; reads at 1x; feels like the course.
concepts.tradeoffs: A post is a modest object; less romantic than a landscape.

concepts.name: Dune, Meadow, Forest
concepts.rationale: A roundel of the course's journey: sand dunes at the foot, a meadow, a skyline of spruce, and the trail winding through all three.
references: The routing through dune, meadow and forest (fact)
concepts.symbolism: The round as a walk: three landscapes, one trail.
concepts.typography: Cormorant Garamond capitals for a quiet, outdoorsy elegance.
concepts.strengths: Says what makes Trails different from the ocean courses.
concepts.tradeoffs: A landscape vignette is more scene than symbol.

recommendation: Concept 1. The carved post is a cleaner, more ownable mark; the roundel would make a fine scorecard cover.
